subject: geography
title: Rivers & Coasts Adventure: Landforms
welcome_lead: From thundering waterfalls to delicate spits — let's tour the landforms erosion and deposition build.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography river and coast landforms — waterfalls, meanders, headlands, stacks, spits.
final_note: You can sketch and explain key river and coastal landforms.

concepts.def: Hard rock over soft rock — soft erodes faster
Bend in a river — eroded outside, deposited inside
Cut-off meander loop, abandoned by river
Hard rock sticking out into the sea
Isolated rock pillar offshore from an old arch
Long sand/shingle ridge into sea (longshore drift)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Where a band of hard rock overlies soft rock, the soft rock is eroded faster. The hard rock is undercut and collapses.

The waterfall retreats upstream over thousands of years — leaving a steep-sided gorge (e.g. High Force on the River Tees).

In the middle course, water flows fastest on the OUTSIDE of bends — eroding a steep river cliff.

It flows slowly on the INSIDE — depositing a slip-off slope.

Bends grow until the river cuts straight through the neck. The old loop is abandoned as an ox-bow lake.

Headlands and bays: discordant coastlines — soft rock erodes back into bays, hard rock juts out as headlands.

Cave → arch → stack → stump: erosion of a headland (e.g. Old Harry Rocks, Dorset).

Spit: longshore drift moves sediment along the coast; where coast bends, sediment carries on — building a long sandy finger (Spurn Head).

mcqs.q: How does an OX-BOW LAKE form?
options: Glacier melts in a hollow
A meander loop is cut off when the neck is breached
The sea floods a valley
A volcano collapses

mcqs.q: Which sequence shows the EROSION of a headland correctly?
options: Stack → arch → cave
Cave → arch → stack → stump
Stump → arch → cave
Spit → cave → bar
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
The zigzag movement of sediment along a coast caused by waves approaching at an angle (swash up the beach) and gravity returning water perpendicular (backwash).
Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
Sand moves along the beach because tides pull it sideways.

mcqs.q: How do waves erode a cliff?
options: Through hydraulic action (water compressing air in cracks), abrasion (waves throwing rocks against cliffs), attrition (rocks smashing against each other), and solution.
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
Waves erode cliffs by pushing water against the rock until it breaks.
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.

mcqs.q: Why do meanders migrate across a floodplain?
options: Faster water on the outside of the bend causes erosion (river cliff); slower water on the inside causes deposition (slip-off slope) — over time the channel shifts laterally.
Meanders form because rivers flow around obstacles like rocks.
Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
Cliffs erode because of acid rain dissolving them.
